pr.title: Build the server with the VS2026 v145 toolset as C++20 with /permissive-
pr.body:
## Summary

Phase 0b of the modernization roadmap. The server moves from the Visual Studio 2019 v142 compiler to the **Visual Studio 2026 v145 compiler**, compiled as **C++20** with **standard conformance (`/permissive-`)**.

## Build changes

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Toolset | v142 (14.29) | **v145** (VS2026 default, 14.5x) |
| Language | default (C++14) | **C++20** |
| Conformance | `/permissive` | **`/permissive-`** |
| Windows target | `_WIN32_WINNT 0x0600` (Vista) | **`0x0A00` (Windows 10)**, matching the installer |
| Boost | built with `msvc-14.2` (`vc142`) | `msvc-14.5` (`vc145`) |
| CI | installs and caches ATL and the 14.29 redist for v142 | **nothing to install**: the image has ATL and the Spectre libraries for v145; the workflow just checks they're there |
| Portable core (GCC/Clang) | C++17 | C++20 |

`IntDir` is pinned to the old default. VS2026 adds `$(ProjectName)\`, which moved `hMailServer.tlb` away from where the tools, installer and post-build expect it.

## Code fixes (C++20 and `/permissive-`)

The fixes are small and don't change behavior, with two exceptions noted below.
- `std::binary_function`, `std::unary_function` and `std::bind2nd` (removed in C++17) are replaced in `StdString.h`.
- `long` overloads for `IntToString`, `AddParameter` and `FormatArgument`, which were ambiguous between `int` and `__int64`.
- Pointer comparisons like `> 0` / `< 0` are written as the null checks they are.
- `typename`, `this->`, unqualified member declarations, and destructor names.
- Non-const reference default arguments, ambiguous `?:` results, `CComQIPtr` direct initialization, and `const_cast` for Windows API string fields.
- `SQLCEConnection.cpp` alone gets `/Zc:strictStrings-`, because Microsoft's vendored `sqlce_sync.h` defaults a `BSTR` to `L""`.
- **`stdafx.h` hard-coded `BOOST_USE_WINAPI_VERSION 0x0600`.** Boost 1.92's Atomic uses `WaitOnAddress` (Windows 8+), so that override is removed.

**Latent bugs found along the way:**
- `XMLite.cpp` `GetText()` streamed `wchar_t*` into a narrow stream. That printed the **pointer address** instead of the text. It now writes the text.
- `SynchronousConnection.cpp` had a global `using namespace boost::system;`. It's removed and the names are qualified.

## Tests

✅ CI [Build run](https://github.com/jassifx/arzoiemail/actions/runs/40022193881):
- Server, tools and installer built.
- Regression suite: **1,168 passed, 0 failed** (same 34 inconclusive and 75 skipped as before). That's the previous baseline of 1,165 plus the 3 `InstallationLayout` tests.
- `InstallationLayout` now requires a runtime of **14.50 or later**.

## Not in this PR

The hardening flags (`/sdl`, `/guard:cf`, `/Qspectre`, `/CETCOMPAT`) come next, as their own PR.

commit.message:
Build the server with the VS2026 v145 toolset as C++20

- PlatformToolset v142 -> v145 (the Visual Studio 2026 default compiler) for
  hMailServer and hMailServer.Minidump, with LanguageStandard stdcpp20. C++20 turns
  /permissive- on; ConformanceMode stays off for now so that strict conformance is
  its own change.
- Boost is built with msvc-14.5 (libboost_*-vc145-*), matching the projects; the
  cache key and the staged-library check follow. msvc-14.2 stays available as an
  option of build-boost.ps1.
- CI no longer installs and caches ATL and the 14.29 redistributable for v142: the
  image carries ATL and the Spectre-mitigated libraries for v145. The workflow now
  checks that the default toolset is 14.5x and has them.
- The oldest runtime the installer may ship is now 14.50; the InstallationLayout
  test follows.
- The portable core builds as C++20 too.
- README, AGENTS.md and the upgrade-boost skill describe the new toolset.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

StdString.h: drop std::unary_function, std::binary_function and std::bind2nd

C++17 removed them and MSVC no longer declares them under /std:c++20. The base
classes only supplied argument and result typedefs that nothing uses; the one
std::bind2nd becomes a lambda.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix the remaining C++20 compile errors

- XMLite.cpp: GetText() streamed LPCTSTR (wchar_t*, since UNICODE is defined) into a
  narrow std::ostringstream. Before C++20 that resolved to operator<<(const void*) and
  wrote the pointer's address instead of the text; C++20 deletes the overload. Use a
  TCHAR stream, so it writes the text.
- SynchronousConnection.cpp: drop the global 'using namespace boost::system'. Under
  /permissive, without two-phase lookup, it made boost::system's operator== overloads
  visible inside Boost.Asio's executor concept checks, which C++20's rewritten
  comparison candidates then broke - so tcp::resolver could no longer be constructed
  from an io_context. The four unqualified error_code uses are now qualified.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Compile the server with standard conformance (/permissive-)

ConformanceMode was left off for the C++20 move, but /permissive turns off two-phase
name lookup, and Boost.Asio's C++20 executor constraints are not evaluated correctly
without it: constructing an ip::tcp::resolver from an io_context failed to find an
any_io_executor constructor. C++20 is meant to be compiled with /permissive-, which is
also what the C++20 default is, so turn it on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix the code /permissive- rejects

- StdString.h: name the dependent base member through this-> (empty()).
- DatabaseConnectionManager.h: a default argument cannot bind a temporary String to a
  non-const reference. The error-message overloads take it explicitly; overloads
  without it supply a local.
- BusinessObject.h, WorkQueue.h: declare members with their plain names inside the
  class, not BusinessObject<T>::BusinessObject / WorkQueue::RemoveRunningTask_.
- BusinessObject.h, Singleton.h: C++20 does not allow a template-id as a destructor
  name (~Singleton<T>).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix the rest of the code C++20 and /permissive- reject

- stdafx.h: target Windows 10 (_WIN32_WINNT 0x0A00) instead of Vista, as the installer
  does. Boost.Atomic uses WaitOnAddress, which needs at least Windows 8.
- Add long overloads to StringParser::IntToString, SQLCommand::AddParameter and
  FormatArgument. long matched the int, unsigned int and __int64 overloads equally well;
  it is 32 bits on Windows, so the new overloads forward to int.
- Ordered comparisons of pointers with 0 (iInsertID > 0, library_instance_ > 0,
  handleFile < 0) were null checks; write them as such.
- Collection.h: typename for a dependent type. CachedObject.h: plain member names.
- ScriptSite.h: direct-initialize CComQIPtr from another interface pointer; pass the
  application name to SysAllocString without T2OLE.
- SURBL.cpp: convert the regex sub_match to a string explicitly.
- XMLite.cpp, SMTPConnection.cpp: give both branches of ?: the same type.
- CertificateVerifier.cpp, hMailServer.cpp: const_cast literals into the non-const string
  members of CERT_ENHKEY_USAGE and SERVICE_TABLE_ENTRY, which Windows only reads.
- SQLCEConnection.cpp: compile with /Zc:strictStrings-, because sqlce_sync.h - vendored
  unchanged from SQL Server Compact - defaults a BSTR parameter to L"".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Pin the Windows API version project-wide; temporarily print what Boost.WinAPI sees

Boost 1.92's Atomic always uses WaitOnAddress on Windows, which Boost.WinAPI only
declares for Windows 8 and later. Define WINVER, _WIN32_WINNT and
BOOST_USE_WINAPI_VERSION (0x0A00, Windows 10) for the whole project, so no header can
see a different value. The #pragma message lines are a temporary diagnostic and will
be removed before this is merged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Let Boost.WinAPI target Windows 10, as the rest of the server does

stdafx.h hard-coded BOOST_USE_WINAPI_VERSION to 0x0600 (Vista), so Boost.WinAPI did not
declare WaitOnAddress, which Boost 1.92's Atomic uses on Windows. Under /permissive-
its templates are parsed where they are defined, so every file that includes
boost/atomic.hpp failed. Remove the override, so Boost takes the version from
_WIN32_WINNT (0x0A00), and drop the previous commit's diagnostics and project-wide
defines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep the server's intermediate directory where VS2022 put it

Visual Studio 2026 defaults IntDir to $(ProjectName)\$(Platform)\$(Configuration)\, which
moved the MIDL-generated hMailServer.tlb out of x64\Release beside hMailServer.exe, where
the tools' interop build, the installer and post-build read it. Pin IntDir to the
previous default, $(Platform)\$(Configuration)\.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
